subject: Staged delivery conditions for FinexCorp enterprise commitment
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@finexcorp.com>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged delivery conditions for FinexCorp enterprise commitment

Folks — looping you in on an ask from FinexCorp that impacts the commercial commitment on HSP-8721. Marta and procurement signaled they will move to a multi-year PO contingent on three delivery milestones rather than a single big-bang feature drop. Their ask (high level):

- M1 (Telemetry export + schema): customer needs a filtered telemetry export (PII-safe) and sample-level tagging within 8 weeks so they can run internal analytics.
- M2 (Per-route metering & billing): ability to surface per-route token metrics + export for billing ingestion in 14 weeks.
- M3 (Model parity + residency fallback): parity with their current model behavior and a residency fallback for 90-day ramp by week 22.

They attached an updated SOW (attached) and are requesting a staged acceptance plan and a limited-credit if we miss a milestone. Procurement copied a partial SOW and asked for a firm delivery commitment tied to payment milestones.

Ask to Product/Eng: can we commit to a staged delivery plan with explicit acceptance criteria per milestone? If not feasible, what are minimal deliverables that would satisfy Finex (e.g., telemetry export + canary) so they will sign?

Key constraints: this is a strategic reference account in US East; they want production telemetry ingestion into their BI stack (no raw PII). They also asked for a 20% uplift on ARR for the additional telemetry SLA.

Please respond with: 1) Feasibility (yes/no), 2) Target milestone list with acceptance criteria, 3) High-level LOE (sprints/heads), and 4) any gating items (security review, DPA, dedicated capacity).

I'll capture responses for the exec approval call Monday.

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged delivery conditions for FinexCorp enterprise commitment

Laura — thanks for the summary. Quick add from the commercial side: Finex is explicitly tying the first payout (30% of TCV) to M1 demo and security sign-off. They pushed back on any solution that would require sharing raw token streams (so filtered exports or aggregated event models only).

Their security lead indicated the telemetry must: 1) drop user identifiers before export, 2) include sampling flags, 3) provide event timestamps with trace ids. Procurement reiterated the desire for a credit of up to 5% of TCV if we miss M2 by more than two weeks.

I'm pasting the snippet of Marta's mail below for context:

"Laura, we can do this if Redwood can commit to a staged delivery and provide a pilot by mid‑June. We need assurances on telemetry redaction and a billing export we can drop into our billing system. Otherwise procurement will push for a holdback in the contract"

I'll drive procurement conversations but need Product/Eng assessment to respond with a proposal.

- Priyom
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged delivery conditions for FinexCorp enterprise commitment

Thanks for the detail — I looked through the SOW and the ask. Short answer: staged delivery is workable, but we need to be explicit about scope, acceptance criteria, and fallbacks. Proposed break-down: 

M1 — Telemetry export (8 weeks)
- Deliverable: filtered export that includes per-request meta (route, model_id, sample_flag, timestamp) with PII-stripping pipeline.
- Acceptance criteria: export lands in Finex's S3 with manifest; 99.9% schema conformity on sample set; security review signed.
- LOE: ~2 devs + 1 infra member, 2 sprints (design) + 2 sprints (implementation) => ~6 weeks active but 8-week calendar given QA and security.

M2 — Per-route metering & billing export (14 weeks)
- Deliverable: per-route token counts, per-model breakdown, and a transform downstream (CSV/JSON) that Finex can ingest.
- Acceptance criteria: nightly export validated against sample dataset; docs; drop-in billing sample for Finex QA.
- LOE: additional 2 sprints (backend/metrics), work overlaps with M1.

M3 — Model parity + residency fallback (22 weeks)
- Deliverable: configuration that maps Finex route behavior to a model variant that reproduces parity; residency fallback for 90‑day ramp.
- Acceptance criteria: parity eval pass on partner-provided test set; rollback plan documented.
- LOE: heavy engineering: ~3–4 sprints including runtime changes, KV cache considerations, and residency ops work.

Gating items:
- Security/compliance (DPA + SOC2 evidence) — needs to be completed before M1 sign-off.
- Dedicated capacity option (Dedicated pool) reduces risk but requires separate commercial terms.
- Instrumentation: we will need Telemetry spec from Finex (PII fields to drop) — suggest Finex fill security-reqs.xlsx we will share.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: telemetry schema drift — mitigate with manifest checks and schema validation.
- Risk: parity regressions — mitigate with evaluation harness and acceptance dataset.

If Sales is comfortable with the staged-credit language, Product is comfortable committing to the milestones above assuming access to Finex test data and a signed DPA. I will get a resource estimate from Eng for heads and sprint allocation tomorrow.

-Irene
VP Product, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marta Ruiz <marta@finexcorp.com>, procurement@finexcorp.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged delivery conditions for FinexCorp enterprise commitment

Appreciate the breakdown, Irene. Procurement and Marta are expecting a tighter calendar — they asked if we can pilot M1 with a limited canary by mid‑June (about 5 weeks). I recognize that shortens the timeline. Two asks from our side to make this realistic:

1) Engineering LOE (heads/sprints) — we need a concrete resource ask we can push to Eng leadership for temporary allocation.
2) Security input — Finex will fill the security-reqs.xlsx (attached); product & eng should confirm whether the DPA + SOC2 evidence checklist is sufficient for sign-off or if they need additional artifacts.

Operational proposal to present to Finex: commit to M1 as a canary (limited traffic, feature-flagged) by June 18th contingent on: signed DPA, Finex provides a sanitized sample dataset, and two dedicated engineers for 6 weeks. If Product/Eng cannot commit, we ask Sales to propose a contractual alternative (extended pilot + higher holdback).

Please respond with the concrete LOE and whether you can accept June 18th as a canary date. If yes, we'll update the SOW and send the DocuSign link to procurement.

Thanks —
Laura
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marta Ruiz <marta@finexcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged delivery conditions for FinexCorp enterprise commitment

Laura/Irene — quick engineering readout and commitment window. We can support a compressed M1 canary by ~June 18th but with clear trade-offs:

Proposed allocation (short term):
- 2 backend engineers (telemetry pipeline + export) — full time for 6 weeks
- 1 infra/ops engineer for S3/connectors and canary plumbing — 4 weeks
- 0.5 QA resource to validate manifests and schema — 4 weeks

Estimated LOE (calendar): 6 weeks active (design + build + canary), total ~8-week calendar if security sign-off slips. If Finex provides sanitized sample data and completes the DPA within 7 business days, we can meet June 18th for a limited canary (restricted routes, <5% traffic).

Technical caveats:
- We will implement a manifest-based export that enforces schema; if Finex adds fields mid-pilot, we will require a change request.
- Parity (M3) requires additional runtime work and is lower-confidence until we run the eval harness; expect an additional ~8–12 weeks after M2.

Commercial recommendation: accept the staged delivery language with a limited holdback (5% of milestone payment) and provide a defined remediation SLA. That reduces legal friction and protects both sides.

If Sales confirms funding for the temporary allocation I will lock the engineers and share a sprint plan by EOD Thursday.

- Ben
Director, Engineering — Runtime & Observability, Redwood Inference
